questions.q: Q.1) Consider the following statements: Other things remaining unchanged market demand for a good might increase if: 1️⃣ Price of its substitute increases 2️⃣ Price of its complement increases 3️⃣ The good is an inferior good and income of the consumers increases 4️⃣ Its price falls. Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Market demand for a good increases if the price of its substitute rises, as consumers switch to the relatively cheaper good. Conversely, an increase in the price of a complement or an increase in income for an inferior good would decrease demand. A fall in the good's own price leads to an increase in the quantity demanded.

questions.q: Q.2) In an economy an increase in the Incremental Capital-Output Ratio (ICOR) primarily indicates:
o: an increase in the marginal productivity of capital within the economy.
the economy is operating at its maximum sustainable productive capacity.
a decline in the efficiency of capital utilization within the economy.
the economy is becoming more efficient in its investment utilization.
questions.e: ICOR indicates the additional unit of capital required to produce an additional unit of output. A higher ICOR value is not preferred because it signifies that production is inefficient, requiring more investment to achieve the same growth. A lower ICOR is beneficial as it indicates efficient capital utilization.

questions.q: Q.3) Palma ratio in an economy is primarily used to measure which among the following?
questions.e: The Palma ratio is a measure of income inequality based on the work of Gabriel Palma. It is defined as the ratio between the income share of the top 10% and the bottom 40% of the population. A higher ratio indicates greater inequality within the society.

questions.q: Q.4) In the context of the Indian economy, which of the following are primary reasons for revising the GDP base year? 1️⃣ Incorporate the structural changes in the economy. 2️⃣ Inflate the GDP value for better fiscal consolidation. 3️⃣ Aligning with international best practices in methodology as recommended by bodies like the UN Statistical Commission 4️⃣ Reflect new spending habits of consumers. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Revising the base year helps capture structural changes like the growth of the service and digital sectors. It aligns India's statistics with UN standards and reflects updated consumer spending patterns. It is not intended to artificially inflate GDP for fiscal purposes.

questions.q: Q.5) In economics, the 'Law of Supply' states that, when all other determinants of supply remain constant, the:
o: quantity supplied of a commodity increases when the income of the consumer increases.
quantity supplied of a commodity decreases when the income of the consumer increases.
quantity supplied of a commodity increases when the price of the commodity increases.
quantity supplied of a commodity decreases when the price of the commodity increases.
questions.e: The Law of Supply states there is a direct relationship between price and quantity supplied. As the price of a product rises, producers are incentivized by higher profits to increase the quantity they bring to the market, assuming other factors like technology and input costs remain constant.

questions.q: Q.6) With reference to the calculation of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) in India, consider the following items: 1️⃣ Capital gains arising from the selling of financial assets. 2️⃣ Brokerage charges earned on the sale of second-hand goods. 3️⃣ Intermediate goods used in manufacturing of final goods. 4️⃣ Government expenditure on construction of the Highways. How many of the items given above are not included in the calculation of GDP?
questions.e: Capital gains are excluded because they reflect changes in asset valuation, not fresh production. Intermediate goods are excluded to avoid double counting. However, brokerage charges are included as they represent a current service, and government infrastructure spending is included as a final investment expenditure.

questions.q: Q.7) In a market, several firms sell pens under different brand names such as Reynolds, Cello, Parker, and Pilot. Although all pens serve the same basic function of writing, they differ in design, ink quality, price, packaging, and brand image. Firms also incur expenditure on advertising to attract customers. Which one of the following market structures described above?
questions.e: Monopolistic competition is characterized by many sellers providing differentiated products that are not perfect substitutes. Key features include branding, advertising, and a limited degree of price-making power, as seen in the varied brands of pens mentioned.

questions.q: Q.8) With reference to consumer behaviour in economics, the term "Veblen Effect" refers to which one of the following?
o: A situation where demand for a good decreases as more and more people own it.
A situation where demand for a good increases because a large number of people are consuming it.
A situation where demand for a good decreases as its price rises due to rejection of conspicuous consumption.
A situation where demand for a good increases with a rise in the price of the good due to its status or prestige value.
questions.e: The Veblen Effect occurs when the demand for a luxury good increases as its price rises because the high price enhances its status or prestige. This is an exception to the law of demand and is closely linked to conspicuous consumption.

questions.q: Q.9) In Country X, residents consume both tea and coffee. After a severe frost in Brazil, coffee prices rise sharply. Consequently, grocery stores in country X report a significant decline in coffee sales and a corresponding increase in the demand for tea, even though the price of tea remains unchanged. The above example best illustrates which of the following concepts?
questions.e: Cross Elasticity of Demand measures how the quantity demanded of one good responds to a change in the price of another. For substitutes like tea and coffee, an increase in the price of coffee leads to an increase in the demand for tea.

questions.q: Q.10) Which of the following statements is correct regarding the recently launched Mutual Credit Guarantee Scheme for MSMEs (MCGS- MSME)?
o: It enables Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) to avail collateral free loans up to Rs.1000 crore.
The funds accessed under this scheme can only be used for meeting operational costs by an MSME.
The Scheme is being implemented by the National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company Limited (NCGTC).
Only Scheduled Commercial Banks are eligible to extend loans under this scheme.
questions.e: The MCGS-MSME is implemented by the NCGTC and enables term loans up to Rs. 100 crore for purchasing equipment or machinery. Eligible lenders include SCBs, AIFIs, and NBFCs. The scheme provides a 60% guarantee for credit facilities.

questions.q: Q.11) Which one of the following was recognised as 'invisible hand' by Adam Smith?
questions.e: Adam Smith introduced the 'invisible hand' concept in 'The Wealth of Nations', referring to the market mechanism. He argued that if individuals are allowed to trade freely, the market naturally moves toward positive outcomes and efficient resource allocation.

questions.q: Q.12) With reference to National Income accounting, consider the following statements: Statement I: In calculation of National Income, the Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) is treated as part of a country's domestic territory. Statement II: A country enjoys exclusive shipping rights in its Exclusive Economic Zone. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Statement I is correct but Statement II is not correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is not correct but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
questions.e: Under UNCLOS, a coastal state has sovereign rights to exploit natural resources in the EEZ, and it is treated as domestic territory for national income. However, it does not have exclusive shipping rights; all countries enjoy freedom of navigation in the EEZ.

questions.q: Q.13) In the context of income method of calculation of National income, consider the following statements: Statement I: Income received from lotteries is not included in estimating National Income. Statement II: Income received from lotteries is a form of transfer income and not factor income. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is not correct but Statement II is correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is not correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
questions.e: The income method only includes factor incomes earned through production services. Lottery winnings are transfer incomes—received without any corresponding production of goods or services—and are therefore excluded from national income estimates.

questions.q: Q.14) The market price of a product is ₹100. The total indirect taxes imposed on it are 25 and total subsidies provided are 10. What is the factor cost of the product?
questions.e: Factor Cost is calculated by subtracting net indirect taxes from the market price. The formula is: Factor Cost = Market Price - Indirect Taxes + Subsidies. In this case, 100 - 25 + 10 = 85.

questions.q: Q.15) Consider the following countries: 1️⃣ Germany 2️⃣ India 3️⃣ UK 4️⃣ Russia. Which of the following is the correct ascending order of the countries given above based on their GDP at current prices in 2025?
questions.e: Based on 2025 GDP estimates at current prices, the ascending order (smallest to largest) is Russia ($2.54 trillion), UK ($3.96 trillion), India ($4.13 trillion), and Germany ($5.01 trillion).

questions.q: Q.16) In which of the following situations will a country's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) be greater than its Gross National Product (GNP)?
o: When income earned by foreign residents within the country exceeds income earned by residents of the country from abroad.
When the country records a surplus in its balance of trade.
When net factor income earned from abroad is positive.
When domestic savings exceed domestic investment.
questions.e: GNP = GDP + Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA). If the income paid to foreign residents domestically is greater than the income residents earn from abroad, NFIA is negative, making GDP larger than GNP.

questions.q: Q.17) With reference to National Income Accounting in India, consider the following taxes: 1️⃣ Stamp duty 2️⃣ Excise duty 3️⃣ Service tax 4️⃣ Custom duty. Which of the above taxes are considered as the product taxes?
questions.e: Product taxes are paid per unit of product, such as excise, service, and custom duties. Production taxes, like stamp duty and land revenue, are paid in relation to production but are independent of the volume of production.

questions.q: Q.18) A newspaper Article in the month of August 2025 read 'A few weeks back, India's Finance Ministry declared the Indian economy to be in a "Goldilocks situation". In this context the Goldilocks situation can be best characterized by?
o: High inflow of foreign investment, Low direct tax rates and subdued inflation.
Moderate growth, Subdued inflation and Supportive monetary conditions.
Low direct tax rates, High inflow of foreign direct investment, High credit deposit ratio of commercial banks.
Moderate growth, Low direct tax rates and High credit deposit ratio of commercial banks.
questions.e: A "Goldilocks situation" is a rare economic state featuring moderate growth, low inflation, and supportive monetary policy. In 2025, India experienced this with 8.2% GDP growth and inflation easing to 0.71% by November.

questions.q: Q.19) Consider the following assets in an economy: 1️⃣ Patents 2️⃣ Goodwill 3️⃣ Software 4️⃣ Inventories 5️⃣ Brand recognition. Which of the above are examples of intangible capital?
o: I, II, III, IV and V
I, II, III and IV only
I, II, III and V only
questions.e: Intangible assets are non-physical rights like patents, goodwill, software, and brand recognition that hold economic value. Inventories are physical stocks of materials or goods and are therefore classified as tangible capital.

questions.q: Q.20) The 'Right to Access to Justice' is protected under which of the following articles of the Constitution of India?
questions.e: In the Anita Kushwaha v. Pushap Sudan  judgment, the Supreme Court ruled that Access to Justice is a Fundamental Right under Article 14 (Equality) and Article 21 (Life and Personal Liberty).

questions.q: Q.21) Which one of the following statements is not correct?
o: When total utility is maximum, marginal utility is zero
When total utility is decreasing, marginal utility is negative
When total utility is maximum, marginal and average utility are equal to each other
When total utility is increasing, marginal utility is positive
questions.e: When total utility is at its maximum, marginal utility (the addition to total utility from one more unit) is zero. However, average utility (total utility divided by units) is still positive and not necessarily equal to marginal utility.

questions.q: Q.22) With reference to the theory of demand and supply in microeconomics, consider the following statements: Statement I: If both the demand and supply curves shift rightward simultaneously, the change in equilibrium price cannot be determined with certainty. Statement II: A rightward shift of the demand curve tends to increase the equilibrium price, whereas a rightward shift of the supply curve tends to decrease the equilibrium price. Which of the above is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is not correct but Statement II is correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is not correct
questions.e: A rightward shift in demand pushes price up, while a rightward shift in supply pushes price down. When both happen at once, the final price depends on which shift is stronger, making the outcome uncertain without more data.

questions.q: Q.23) With reference to macroeconomic analysis, the boundary (or frontier) of a Production Possibility Curve (PPC) represents which of the following?
questions.e: The PPC frontier represents the maximum possible output an economy can produce using all available resources efficiently. This maximum attainable level is referred to as the Potential GDP.

questions.q: Q.24) Suppose the Net National Product at Factor Cost (NNPFC) of a particular country in a year is Rs 1,900 crores. There are no interest payments made by households to firms/government or by firms/government to households. Households' Personal Disposable Income (PDI) is Rs 1,200 crores, with personal income taxes of Rs 600 crores, and retained earnings of firms and government are Rs 200 crores. What is the value of transfer payments made by the government and firms to households?
questions.e: Personal Income (PI) = PDI + Taxes = 1200 + 600 = 1800. Also, PI = NNPFC - Retained Earnings + Transfer Payments. Substituting the values: 1800 = 1900 - 200 + Transfer Payments, which gives Transfer Payments = 100 crore.

questions.q: Q.25) With reference to Fixed Capital in business finance, consider the following: 1️⃣ Money spent on purchase of raw materials. 2️⃣ Finished goods inventory 3️⃣ Expenditure incurred on purchase of Computer. How many of the above are examples of Fixed Capital?
questions.e: Fixed capital consists of long-term assets used repeatedly in production, such as computers. Raw materials and finished goods are current assets used for day-to-day operations and are part of working capital.

questions.q: Q.26) In macroeconomic terms, which of the following best describes the term "Technical Recession'?
o: The prolonged decline in economic activity lasting for a decade.
The contraction in real GDP for two consecutive quarters.
The situation where the inflation rate exceeds the GDP growth rate for two consecutive years.
The condition where the unemployment rate remains high despite positive economic growth.
questions.e: A technical recession is a standard benchmark defined by a contraction (negative growth) in an economy's real Gross Domestic Product (GDP) for two consecutive quarters.

questions.q: Q.27) With reference to economics, what does the term 'Hysteresis' refer to?
o: The transition of an economy directly from agrarian to services.
The policy of ensuring constant inflation in an economy to stabilise economic growth.
A situation which arises when any historical event affects the future economic path.
A rapid recovery in employment immediately after a recession.
questions.e: Hysteresis describes how past economic shocks (like a deep recession) can have long-lasting effects on the future, such as high unemployment persisting even after the economy recovers due to workers losing skills.

questions.q: Q.28) With reference to national income accounting in India, consider the following: 1️⃣ Purchase of machinery and equipment. 2️⃣ Construction of roads and bridges. 3️⃣ Increase in the number of young livestock at dairy farms. 4️⃣ Increase in stocks of unsold finished goods. How many of the above are part of Gross Fixed Capital Formation (GFCF)?
questions.e: GFCF includes additions to fixed assets like machinery, infrastructure (roads/bridges), and productive livestock. Unsold stocks of finished goods are considered inventory investment, which is a separate category from fixed capital formation.

questions.q: Q.29) With reference to the limitations of Gross Domestic Product (GDP), consider the following statements: 1️⃣ A rise in GDP does not necessarily ensure the welfare of citizens. 2️⃣ GDP does not reflect the economic inequality in an economy. 3️⃣ GDP does not account for economic activities of un-registered manufacturing factories in the economy. 4️⃣ GDP does not account for the economic value of environmental resources. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: GDP does not measure income distribution or environmental damage (negative externalities). However, it does attempt to account for the unregistered sector using the workforce and GVA-per-worker method, so statement 3 is incorrect.

questions.q: Q.30) With reference to the production of Makhana in India, consider the following statements: Statement I: More than 80% of India's Makhana is produced by Bihar alone. Statement II: Makhana can be grown only in cool and dry season, thus requiring ample irrigation. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct but Statement II is not correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Statement I is not correct but Statement II is correct
questions.e: Bihar produces about 90% of India's makhana. However, it is a tropical/subtropical crop that thrives in wetlands and stagnant water during warm temperatures ($20-35^{\circ}C$), not just in cool, dry seasons.

questions.q: Q.31) Zero price elasticity of demand means?
o: for a small change in price, there is a small change in demand
for a large change in price, there is a small change in demand
whatever the change in price, there is absolutely no change in demand
for a small change in price, there is a large change in demand
questions.e: Zero price elasticity, or perfectly inelastic demand, occurs when consumers buy the same amount of a good regardless of its price. The demand curve in this case is a vertical line.

questions.q: Q.32) In which of the following situation(s) will the Per Capita Income of a country is/are most likely to increase? 1️⃣ When the rate of GDP growth exceeds the rate of population growth. 2️⃣ When the total population declines while GDP remains constant. 3️⃣ When nominal GDP rises at a faster rate than the inflation rate. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Per Capita Income (PCI) increases if the growth in national income (GDP) outpaces population growth. While statement 3 implies real GDP is rising, PCI won't necessarily increase unless that real growth is also faster than population growth.

questions.q: Q.33) With reference to Giffen goods, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ They are the type of inferior goods. 2️⃣ The demand for the Giffen goods generally increases with increase in its price. 3️⃣ Diamonds are an example of Giffen goods. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Giffen goods are rare inferior goods where demand increases as price rises (upward-sloping demand curve). Diamonds are Veblen goods, which are luxury items consumed for status, not Giffen goods.

questions.q: Q.34) In the context of the Indian economy, consider the following statements about Private Final Consumption Expenditure (PFCE): 1️⃣ It refers to expenditure incurred on the final consumption of goods and services by the resident households and non-profit institutions serving households. 2️⃣ The share of PFCE in India's GDP has been steadily increasing in the last decade. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: PFCE covers final spending by resident households and NPISHs. While it reached a high of 61.5% in FY26, its share in GDP has fluctuated over the last decade rather than showing a steady, continuous increase.

questions.q: Q.35) With reference to the India's Gross Domestic Product (GDP), consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The base year for GDP Estimates has been revised from 2011-12 to 2022-23. 2️⃣ Presently, the National Statistical Office (NSO), Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MOSPI) calculate the quarterly GDP estimates using Benchmark-Indicator. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: India recently revised its GDP base year to 2022-23 to capture the modern economic structure. The NSO uses the benchmark-indicator method, applying high-frequency data to annual benchmarks to estimate quarterly performance.

questions.q: Q.36) Consider the following information: 1️⃣ Public Good: Goods provided by government only to a specified social class (Ex: Government administration) 2️⃣ Free Good: Goods available in abundance without any cost or human effort (Ex: Air) 3️⃣ Club good: Goods that are non-rival in consumption but excludable (Ex: Museum). In how many of the above rows is the given information correctly matched?
questions.e: Public goods are available to all, not just a specific class. Row 1 is incorrect. Row 2 is correct as air is a free good. Row 3 is correct because club goods like museums are non-rival (one's use doesn't stop another's) but you can exclude people via entry fees.

questions.q: Q.37) In macroeconomics, autonomous consumption refers to:
o: Consumption that increases proportionately with income.
Consumption that occurs even when income is zero.
Consumption that cannot be measured in national income accounting.
Consumption of luxury goods after basic needs are satisfied.
questions.e: Autonomous consumption is the minimum level of spending on necessities (food, shelter) that must happen even if current income is zero. It is funded through savings, borrowing, or transfers.

questions.q: Q.38) In the context of the Indian economy, which of the following measures is least likely to be adopted by the Government/RBI during a recession? 1️⃣ Increasing the expenditure on infrastructure projects 2️⃣ Increasing the reverse repo rate 3️⃣ Introduction of new public welfare schemes 4️⃣ Increasing the indirect tax rates. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: During a recession, the aim is to boost liquidity and demand. Increasing the reverse repo rate (which pulls money out of the system) and raising indirect taxes (which makes goods more expensive) would hurt the economy further and are unlikely to be done.

questions.q: Q.39) In the context of an economy, the Solow Paradox refers to which of the following situations?
o: The phenomenon of the rapid growth in the manufacturing sector despite low public investment.
The phenomenon of inflow of high remittances despite a slowdown in global economic growth.
The phenomenon of extensive use of advanced technology without an expected increase in productivity
The phenomenon of the continuous depreciation of a country's currency despite strong macroeconomic fundamentals.
questions.e: Robert Solow observed that "the computer age is everywhere except in the productivity statistics." This paradox describes periods where massive investment in technology fails to show up as measurable gains in economic productivity.

questions.q: Q.40) Consider the following countries: 1️⃣ Kazakhstan 2️⃣ Turkey 3️⃣ Russia 4️⃣ Iran 5️⃣ Afghanistan. How many of the above countries share their borders with the Caspian Sea?
questions.e: The Caspian Sea is bordered by five countries: Russia, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, and Iran. From the list provided, only Kazakhstan, Russia, and Iran share a border. Turkey and Afghanistan do not.

questions.q: Q.41) Multipliers will be lower with which one of the following?
questions.e: The multiplier effect depends on how much of new income is spent. If the Marginal Propensity to Consume (MPC) is low, people save more of their income instead of spending it, leading to a smaller overall increase in economic activity (a lower multiplier).

questions.q: Q.42) With reference to GDP Deflator, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It is calculated as the ratio of Nominal GDP to Real GDP. 2️⃣ If the value of the GDP Deflator is less than 1, it indicates deflation in the economy. 3️⃣ It does not include the price of imported goods and services. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The GDP deflator is a broad measure of inflation (Nominal/Real GDP). A value below 1 indicates prices are lower than the base year (deflation). Unlike the CPI, the GDP deflator only tracks goods produced domestically, excluding imports.

questions.q: Q.43) Consider the following statements: Statement I: Net National Product at Factor Cost (NNP at FC) is considered the best measure of national income of a country. Statement II: It includes net factor income earned from abroad. Statement III: It excludes depreciation from the value of output. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement II and Statement III are correct but only one of them explains Statement I
Both Statement II and Statement III are correct and both of them explain Statement I
Neither Statement II nor Statement III is correct
Only one of the Statements II and III is correct and that explains Statement I
questions.e: NNP at FC is the most accurate measure because it accounts for income from abroad (NFIA) and removes the "wear and tear" of capital (depreciation). These adjustments ensure it reflects the true income available to a nation's residents.

questions.q: Q.44) Consider the following scenarios regarding the provision of public goods and services: 1️⃣ A public sector company manufacturing aluminium using its idle machinery and labour for the production of certain other goods. 2️⃣ The Central Government conducts free skill-development workshops for unemployed youth using volunteer trainers and existing government school classrooms after regular hours. 3️⃣ The state government distributes the excess food grains, which were otherwise rotting, to certain households. In which of the above scenarios is/are the Opportunity cost will be zero?
questions.e: Opportunity cost is rarely zero. Idle machines still depreciate when used, volunteers' time could be used elsewhere, and distributing "rotting" food requires transport and labor resources that have alternative uses.

questions.q: Q.45) With reference to national income accounting in India, consider the following statements regarding Consumption of Fixed Capital: 1️⃣ It refers to the normal wear and tear of fixed capital assets during a year. 2️⃣ It does not take into account losses of fixed capital arising from unforeseen events such as fire, earthquake or floods. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Consumption of Fixed Capital (CFC) represents expected depreciation from regular use. Capital Loss from unexpected disasters like floods or fires is a separate concept and is not included in CFC.

questions.q: Q.46) Passage Crux: "Cyber parenting involves preparing children... This balance can only be achieved when parents themselves are aware of both the positive and negative effects..." Which statement reflects the crux?
o: Parents need to understand the benefits and risks of the digital world to help their children navigate it safely.
Parents should encourage their children to nurture meaningful real life relationships.
Children are strongly attracted to the latest trends circulating on social media platforms.
As technology has become a part of modern-day life, children need to be taught the pros and cons of using it.
questions.e: The passage emphasizes that digital parenting requires parents to be well-informed about the digital world's effects so they can effectively guide their children toward a balanced life.

questions.q: Q.47) Passage Inference: Himalayan towns face water stress due to tourist surges and structural fragility... "The situation demands a reorientation of planning frameworks..." Which is the logical inference?
o: Water scarcity in tourist destinations stems from governance deficiencies in water management.
Heavy tourist influx has led to growing water scarcity in destinations across the globe.
Low water availability in the Himalayas is being further aggravated by pressure from tourism.
Planners need to balance the growing water demands of the tourism industry with the limited resources in the Himalayas.
questions.e: The passage concludes that current planning must change to align tourism growth with the actual hydrological limits and environmental sustainability of the fragile Himalayan region.

questions.q: Q.48) Based on the passage regarding Himalayan water crises, consider these assumptions: 1️⃣ The number of tourists in Himalayan towns must be capped. 2️⃣ Economic growth must align with the principles of environmental sustainability. Which are valid?
questions.e: While the passage calls for aligning growth with hydrological limits, it doesn't explicitly state that "capping" numbers is the required measure. However, it directly advocates for environmental sustainability in planning.

questions.q: Q.49) If $M=100!+101!+102!$ then consider: 1️⃣ The largest prime factor of M is 101. 2️⃣ The number of trailing zeros in M is 24. 3️⃣ M is divisible by $^{2}$. Which are correct?
questions.e: M simplifies to $100! \times 10404$. Since 10404 is $2^{2} \times 3^{2} \times 17^{2}$, it adds no new prime factors above 100. 100! has 24 trailing zeros, and since 10404 has no factors of 5, the total remains 24. 103 is not a factor of $M$.

questions.q: Q.50) The difference between any two natural numbers is 10. What can be said about the natural numbers which are divisible by 5 and lie between these two numbers?
o: There can be more than one such number.
There is only one such number.
There are only two such numbers.
questions.e: If the numbers are 5 and 15, there is only one multiple of 5  between them. If the numbers are 1 and 11, there are two (5 and 10). Thus, there can be more than one such number depending on the starting value.

questions.q: Q.1) Consider the following statements: Other things remaining unchanged market demand for a good might increase if: 1️⃣ Price of its substitute increases 2️⃣ Price of its complement increases 3️⃣ The good is an inferior good and income of the consumers increases 4️⃣ Its price falls. Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Market demand for a good increases if the price of its substitute rises, as consumers switch to the relatively cheaper good. Conversely, an increase in the price of a complement or an increase in income for an inferior good would decrease demand. A fall in the good's own price leads to an increase in the quantity demanded.

questions.q: Q.2) In an economy an increase in the Incremental Capital-Output Ratio (ICOR) primarily indicates:
o: the economy is becoming more efficient in its investment utilization.
the economy is operating at its maximum sustainable productive capacity.
an increase in the marginal productivity of capital within the economy.
a decline in the efficiency of capital utilization within the economy.
questions.e: ICOR indicates the additional unit of capital required to produce an additional unit of output. A higher ICOR value is not preferred because it signifies that production is inefficient, requiring more investment to achieve the same growth. A lower ICOR is beneficial as it indicates efficient capital utilization.

questions.q: Q.3) Palma ratio in an economy is primarily used to measure which among the following?
questions.e: The Palma ratio is a measure of income inequality based on the work of Gabriel Palma. It is defined as the ratio between the income share of the top 10% and the bottom 40% of the population. A higher ratio indicates greater inequality within the society.

questions.q: Q.4) In the context of the Indian economy, which of the following are primary reasons for revising the GDP base year? 1️⃣ Incorporate the structural changes in the economy. 2️⃣ Inflate the GDP value for better fiscal consolidation. 3️⃣ Aligning with international best practices in methodology as recommended by bodies like the UN Statistical Commission 4️⃣ Reflect new spending habits of consumers. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Revising the base year helps capture structural changes like the growth of the service and digital sectors. It aligns India's statistics with UN standards and reflects updated consumer spending patterns. It is not intended to artificially inflate GDP for fiscal purposes.

questions.q: Q.5) In economics, the 'Law of Supply' states that, when all other determinants of supply remain constant, the:
o: quantity supplied of a commodity increases when the income of the consumer increases.
quantity supplied of a commodity decreases when the income of the consumer increases.
quantity supplied of a commodity increases when the price of the commodity increases.
quantity supplied of a commodity decreases when the price of the commodity increases.
questions.e: The Law of Supply states there is a direct relationship between price and quantity supplied. As the price of a product rises, producers are incentivized by higher profits to increase the quantity they bring to the market, assuming other factors like technology and input costs remain constant.

questions.q: Q.6) With reference to the calculation of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) in India, consider the following items: 1️⃣ Capital gains arising from the selling of financial assets. 2️⃣ Brokerage charges earned on the sale of second-hand goods. 3️⃣ Intermediate goods used in manufacturing of final goods. 4️⃣ Government expenditure on construction of the Highways. How many of the items given above are not included in the calculation of GDP?
questions.e: Capital gains are excluded because they reflect changes in asset valuation, not fresh production. Intermediate goods are excluded to avoid double counting. However, brokerage charges are included as they represent a current service, and government infrastructure spending is included as a final investment expenditure.

questions.q: Q.7) In a market, several firms sell pens under different brand names such as Reynolds, Cello, Parker, and Pilot. Although all pens serve the same basic function of writing, they differ in design, ink quality, price, packaging, and brand image. Firms also incur expenditure on advertising to attract customers. Which one of the following market structures described above?
questions.e: Monopolistic competition is characterized by many sellers providing differentiated products that are not perfect substitutes. Key features include branding, advertising, and a limited degree of price-making power, as seen in the varied brands of pens mentioned.

questions.q: Q.8) With reference to consumer behaviour in economics, the term "Veblen Effect" refers to which one of the following?
o: A situation where demand for a good increases with a rise in the price of the good due to its status or prestige value.
A situation where demand for a good decreases as more and more people own it.
A situation where demand for a good increases because a large number of people are consuming it.
A situation where demand for a good decreases as its price rises due to rejection of conspicuous consumption.
questions.e: The Veblen Effect occurs when the demand for a luxury good increases as its price rises because the high price enhances its status or prestige. This is an exception to the law of demand and is closely linked to conspicuous consumption.

questions.q: Q.9) In Country X, residents consume both tea and coffee. After a severe frost in Brazil, coffee prices rise sharply. Consequently, grocery stores in country X report a significant decline in coffee sales and a corresponding increase in the demand for tea, even though the price of tea remains unchanged. The above example best illustrates which of the following concepts?
questions.e: Cross Elasticity of Demand measures how the quantity demanded of one good responds to a change in the price of another. For substitutes like tea and coffee, an increase in the price of coffee leads to an increase in the demand for tea.

questions.q: Q.10) Which of the following statements is correct regarding the recently launched Mutual Credit Guarantee Scheme for MSMEs (MCGS- MSME)?
o: The Scheme is being implemented by the National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company Limited (NCGTC).
Only Scheduled Commercial Banks are eligible to extend loans under this scheme.
The funds accessed under this scheme can only be used for meeting operational costs by an MSME.
It enables Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) to avail collateral free loans up to Rs.1000 crore.
questions.e: The MCGS-MSME is implemented by the NCGTC and enables term loans up to Rs. 100 crore for purchasing equipment or machinery. Eligible lenders include SCBs, AIFIs, and NBFCs. The scheme provides a 60% guarantee for credit facilities.

questions.q: Q.11) Which one of the following was recognised as 'invisible hand' by Adam Smith?
questions.e: Adam Smith introduced the 'invisible hand' concept in 'The Wealth of Nations', referring to the market mechanism. He argued that if individuals are allowed to trade freely, the market naturally moves toward positive outcomes and efficient resource allocation.

questions.q: Q.12) With reference to National Income accounting, consider the following statements: Statement I: In calculation of National Income, the Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) is treated as part of a country's domestic territory. Statement II: A country enjoys exclusive shipping rights in its Exclusive Economic Zone. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is not correct but Statement II is correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is not correct
questions.e: Under UNCLOS, a coastal state has sovereign rights to exploit natural resources in the EEZ, and it is treated as domestic territory for national income. However, it does not have exclusive shipping rights; all countries enjoy freedom of navigation in the EEZ.

questions.q: Q.13) In the context of income method of calculation of National income, consider the following statements: Statement I: Income received from lotteries is not included in estimating National Income. Statement II: Income received from lotteries is a form of transfer income and not factor income. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct but Statement II is not correct
Statement I is not correct but Statement II is correct
questions.e: The income method only includes factor incomes earned through production services. Lottery winnings are transfer incomes—received without any corresponding production of goods or services—and are therefore excluded from national income estimates.

questions.q: Q.14) The market price of a product is ₹100. The total indirect taxes imposed on it are 25 and total subsidies provided are 10. What is the factor cost of the product?
questions.e: Factor Cost is calculated by subtracting net indirect taxes from the market price. The formula is: Factor Cost = Market Price - Indirect Taxes + Subsidies. In this case, 100 - 25 + 10 = 85.

questions.q: Q.15) Consider the following countries: 1️⃣ Germany 2️⃣ India 3️⃣ UK 4️⃣ Russia. Which of the following is the correct ascending order of the countries given above based on their GDP at current prices in 2025?
questions.e: Based on 2025 GDP estimates at current prices, the ascending order (smallest to largest) is Russia ($2.54 trillion), UK ($3.96 trillion), India ($4.13 trillion), and Germany ($5.01 trillion).

questions.q: Q.16) In which of the following situations will a country's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) be greater than its Gross National Product (GNP)?
o: When the country records a surplus in its balance of trade.
When income earned by foreign residents within the country exceeds income earned by residents of the country from abroad.
When net factor income earned from abroad is positive.
When domestic savings exceed domestic investment.
questions.e: GNP = GDP + Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA). If the income paid to foreign residents domestically is greater than the income residents earn from abroad, NFIA is negative, making GDP larger than GNP.

questions.q: Q.17) With reference to National Income Accounting in India, consider the following taxes: 1️⃣ Stamp duty 2️⃣ Excise duty 3️⃣ Service tax 4️⃣ Custom duty. Which of the above taxes are considered as the product taxes?
questions.e: Product taxes are paid per unit of product, such as excise, service, and custom duties. Production taxes, like stamp duty and land revenue, are paid in relation to production but are independent of the volume of production.

questions.q: Q.18) A newspaper Article in the month of August 2025 read 'A few weeks back, India's Finance Ministry declared the Indian economy to be in a "Goldilocks situation". In this context the Goldilocks situation can be best characterized by?
o: Moderate growth, Low direct tax rates and High credit deposit ratio of commercial banks.
High inflow of foreign investment, Low direct tax rates and subdued inflation.
Low direct tax rates, High inflow of foreign direct investment, High credit deposit ratio of commercial banks.
Moderate growth, Subdued inflation and Supportive monetary conditions.
questions.e: A "Goldilocks situation" is a rare economic state featuring moderate growth, low inflation, and supportive monetary policy. In 2025, India experienced this with 8.2% GDP growth and inflation easing to 0.71% by November.

questions.q: Q.19) Consider the following assets in an economy: 1️⃣ Patents 2️⃣ Goodwill 3️⃣ Software 4️⃣ Inventories 5️⃣ Brand recognition. Which of the above are examples of intangible capital?
o: I, II, III, IV and V
I, II, III and IV only
I, II, III and V only
questions.e: Intangible assets are non-physical rights like patents, goodwill, software, and brand recognition that hold economic value. Inventories are physical stocks of materials or goods and are therefore classified as tangible capital.

questions.q: Q.20) The 'Right to Access to Justice' is protected under which of the following articles of the Constitution of India?
questions.e: In the Anita Kushwaha v. Pushap Sudan  judgment, the Supreme Court ruled that Access to Justice is a Fundamental Right under Article 14 (Equality) and Article 21 (Life and Personal Liberty).

questions.q: Q.21) Which one of the following statements is not correct?
o: When total utility is maximum, marginal and average utility are equal to each other
When total utility is increasing, marginal utility is positive
When total utility is maximum, marginal utility is zero
When total utility is decreasing, marginal utility is negative
questions.e: When total utility is at its maximum, marginal utility (the addition to total utility from one more unit) is zero. However, average utility (total utility divided by units) is still positive and not necessarily equal to marginal utility.

questions.q: Q.22) With reference to the theory of demand and supply in microeconomics, consider the following statements: Statement I: If both the demand and supply curves shift rightward simultaneously, the change in equilibrium price cannot be determined with certainty. Statement II: A rightward shift of the demand curve tends to increase the equilibrium price, whereas a rightward shift of the supply curve tends to decrease the equilibrium price. Which of the above is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Statement I is correct but Statement II is not correct
Statement I is not correct but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
questions.e: A rightward shift in demand pushes price up, while a rightward shift in supply pushes price down. When both happen at once, the final price depends on which shift is stronger, making the outcome uncertain without more data.

questions.q: Q.23) With reference to macroeconomic analysis, the boundary (or frontier) of a Production Possibility Curve (PPC) represents which of the following?
questions.e: The PPC frontier represents the maximum possible output an economy can produce using all available resources efficiently. This maximum attainable level is referred to as the Potential GDP.

questions.q: Q.24) Suppose the Net National Product at Factor Cost (NNPFC) of a particular country in a year is Rs 1,900 crores. There are no interest payments made by households to firms/government or by firms/government to households. Households' Personal Disposable Income (PDI) is Rs 1,200 crores, with personal income taxes of Rs 600 crores, and retained earnings of firms and government are Rs 200 crores. What is the value of transfer payments made by the government and firms to households?
questions.e: Personal Income (PI) = PDI + Taxes = 1200 + 600 = 1800. Also, PI = NNPFC - Retained Earnings + Transfer Payments. Substituting the values: 1800 = 1900 - 200 + Transfer Payments, which gives Transfer Payments = 100 crore.

questions.q: Q.25) With reference to Fixed Capital in business finance, consider the following: 1️⃣ Money spent on purchase of raw materials. 2️⃣ Finished goods inventory 3️⃣ Expenditure incurred on purchase of Computer. How many of the above are examples of Fixed Capital?
questions.e: Fixed capital consists of long-term assets used repeatedly in production, such as computers. Raw materials and finished goods are current assets used for day-to-day operations and are part of working capital.

questions.q: Q.26) In macroeconomic terms, which of the following best describes the term "Technical Recession'?
o: The situation where the inflation rate exceeds the GDP growth rate for two consecutive years.
The prolonged decline in economic activity lasting for a decade.
The condition where the unemployment rate remains high despite positive economic growth.
The contraction in real GDP for two consecutive quarters.
questions.e: A technical recession is a standard benchmark defined by a contraction (negative growth) in an economy's real Gross Domestic Product (GDP) for two consecutive quarters.

questions.q: Q.27) With reference to economics, what does the term 'Hysteresis' refer to?
o: The transition of an economy directly from agrarian to services.
The policy of ensuring constant inflation in an economy to stabilise economic growth.
A rapid recovery in employment immediately after a recession.
A situation which arises when any historical event affects the future economic path.
questions.e: Hysteresis describes how past economic shocks (like a deep recession) can have long-lasting effects on the future, such as high unemployment persisting even after the economy recovers due to workers losing skills.

questions.q: Q.28) With reference to national income accounting in India, consider the following: 1️⃣ Purchase of machinery and equipment. 2️⃣ Construction of roads and bridges. 3️⃣ Increase in the number of young livestock at dairy farms. 4️⃣ Increase in stocks of unsold finished goods. How many of the above are part of Gross Fixed Capital Formation (GFCF)?
questions.e: GFCF includes additions to fixed assets like machinery, infrastructure (roads/bridges), and productive livestock. Unsold stocks of finished goods are considered inventory investment, which is a separate category from fixed capital formation.

questions.q: Q.29) With reference to the limitations of Gross Domestic Product (GDP), consider the following statements: 1️⃣ A rise in GDP does not necessarily ensure the welfare of citizens. 2️⃣ GDP does not reflect the economic inequality in an economy. 3️⃣ GDP does not account for economic activities of un-registered manufacturing factories in the economy. 4️⃣ GDP does not account for the economic value of environmental resources. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: GDP does not measure income distribution or environmental damage (negative externalities). However, it does attempt to account for the unregistered sector using the workforce and GVA-per-worker method, so statement 3 is incorrect.

questions.q: Q.30) With reference to the production of Makhana in India, consider the following statements: Statement I: More than 80% of India's Makhana is produced by Bihar alone. Statement II: Makhana can be grown only in cool and dry season, thus requiring ample irrigation. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Statement I is not correct but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct but Statement II is not correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
questions.e: Bihar produces about 90% of India's makhana. However, it is a tropical/subtropical crop that thrives in wetlands and stagnant water during warm temperatures ($20-35^{\circ}C$), not just in cool, dry seasons.

questions.q: Q.31) Zero price elasticity of demand means?
o: for a small change in price, there is a large change in demand
for a small change in price, there is a small change in demand
for a large change in price, there is a small change in demand
whatever the change in price, there is absolutely no change in demand
questions.e: Zero price elasticity, or perfectly inelastic demand, occurs when consumers buy the same amount of a good regardless of its price. The demand curve in this case is a vertical line.

questions.q: Q.32) In which of the following situation(s) will the Per Capita Income of a country is/are most likely to increase? 1️⃣ When the rate of GDP growth exceeds the rate of population growth. 2️⃣ When the total population declines while GDP remains constant. 3️⃣ When nominal GDP rises at a faster rate than the inflation rate. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Per Capita Income (PCI) increases if the growth in national income (GDP) outpaces population growth. While statement 3 implies real GDP is rising, PCI won't necessarily increase unless that real growth is also faster than population growth.

questions.q: Q.33) With reference to Giffen goods, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ They are the type of inferior goods. 2️⃣ The demand for the Giffen goods generally increases with increase in its price. 3️⃣ Diamonds are an example of Giffen goods. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Giffen goods are rare inferior goods where demand increases as price rises (upward-sloping demand curve). Diamonds are Veblen goods, which are luxury items consumed for status, not Giffen goods.

questions.q: Q.34) In the context of the Indian economy, consider the following statements about Private Final Consumption Expenditure (PFCE): 1️⃣ It refers to expenditure incurred on the final consumption of goods and services by the resident households and non-profit institutions serving households. 2️⃣ The share of PFCE in India's GDP has been steadily increasing in the last decade. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: PFCE covers final spending by resident households and NPISHs. While it reached a high of 61.5% in FY26, its share in GDP has fluctuated over the last decade rather than showing a steady, continuous increase.

questions.q: Q.35) With reference to the India's Gross Domestic Product (GDP), consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The base year for GDP Estimates has been revised from 2011-12 to 2022-23. 2️⃣ Presently, the National Statistical Office (NSO), Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MOSPI) calculate the quarterly GDP estimates using Benchmark-Indicator. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: India recently revised its GDP base year to 2022-23 to capture the modern economic structure. The NSO uses the benchmark-indicator method, applying high-frequency data to annual benchmarks to estimate quarterly performance.

questions.q: Q.36) Consider the following information: 1️⃣ Public Good: Goods provided by government only to a specified social class (Ex: Government administration) 2️⃣ Free Good: Goods available in abundance without any cost or human effort (Ex: Air) 3️⃣ Club good: Goods that are non-rival in consumption but excludable (Ex: Museum). In how many of the above rows is the given information correctly matched?
questions.e: Public goods are available to all, not just a specific class. Row 1 is incorrect. Row 2 is correct as air is a free good. Row 3 is correct because club goods like museums are non-rival (one's use doesn't stop another's) but you can exclude people via entry fees.

questions.q: Q.37) In macroeconomics, autonomous consumption refers to:
o: Consumption that cannot be measured in national income accounting.
Consumption that increases proportionately with income.
Consumption of luxury goods after basic needs are satisfied.
Consumption that occurs even when income is zero.
questions.e: Autonomous consumption is the minimum level of spending on necessities (food, shelter) that must happen even if current income is zero. It is funded through savings, borrowing, or transfers.

questions.q: Q.38) In the context of the Indian economy, which of the following measures is least likely to be adopted by the Government/RBI during a recession? 1️⃣ Increasing the expenditure on infrastructure projects 2️⃣ Increasing the reverse repo rate 3️⃣ Introduction of new public welfare schemes 4️⃣ Increasing the indirect tax rates. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: During a recession, the aim is to boost liquidity and demand. Increasing the reverse repo rate (which pulls money out of the system) and raising indirect taxes (which makes goods more expensive) would hurt the economy further and are unlikely to be done.

questions.q: Q.39) In the context of an economy, the Solow Paradox refers to which of the following situations?
o: The phenomenon of extensive use of advanced technology without an expected increase in productivity
The phenomenon of the continuous depreciation of a country's currency despite strong macroeconomic fundamentals.
The phenomenon of inflow of high remittances despite a slowdown in global economic growth.
The phenomenon of the rapid growth in the manufacturing sector despite low public investment.
questions.e: Robert Solow observed that "the computer age is everywhere except in the productivity statistics." This paradox describes periods where massive investment in technology fails to show up as measurable gains in economic productivity.

questions.q: Q.40) Consider the following countries: 1️⃣ Kazakhstan 2️⃣ Turkey 3️⃣ Russia 4️⃣ Iran 5️⃣ Afghanistan. How many of the above countries share their borders with the Caspian Sea?
questions.e: The Caspian Sea is bordered by five countries: Russia, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, and Iran. From the list provided, only Kazakhstan, Russia, and Iran share a border. Turkey and Afghanistan do not.

questions.q: Q.41) Multipliers will be lower with which one of the following?
questions.e: The multiplier effect depends on how much of new income is spent. If the Marginal Propensity to Consume (MPC) is low, people save more of their income instead of spending it, leading to a smaller overall increase in economic activity (a lower multiplier).

questions.q: Q.42) With reference to GDP Deflator, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It is calculated as the ratio of Nominal GDP to Real GDP. 2️⃣ If the value of the GDP Deflator is less than 1, it indicates deflation in the economy. 3️⃣ It does not include the price of imported goods and services. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The GDP deflator is a broad measure of inflation (Nominal/Real GDP). A value below 1 indicates prices are lower than the base year (deflation). Unlike the CPI, the GDP deflator only tracks goods produced domestically, excluding imports.

questions.q: Q.43) Consider the following statements: Statement I: Net National Product at Factor Cost (NNP at FC) is considered the best measure of national income of a country. Statement II: It includes net factor income earned from abroad. Statement III: It excludes depreciation from the value of output. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement II and Statement III are correct and both of them explain Statement I
Neither Statement II nor Statement III is correct
Both Statement II and Statement III are correct but only one of them explains Statement I
Only one of the Statements II and III is correct and that explains Statement I
questions.e: NNP at FC is the most accurate measure because it accounts for income from abroad (NFIA) and removes the "wear and tear" of capital (depreciation). These adjustments ensure it reflects the true income available to a nation's residents.

questions.q: Q.44) Consider the following scenarios regarding the provision of public goods and services: 1️⃣ A public sector company manufacturing aluminium using its idle machinery and labour for the production of certain other goods. 2️⃣ The Central Government conducts free skill-development workshops for unemployed youth using volunteer trainers and existing government school classrooms after regular hours. 3️⃣ The state government distributes the excess food grains, which were otherwise rotting, to certain households. In which of the above scenarios is/are the Opportunity cost will be zero?
questions.e: Opportunity cost is rarely zero. Idle machines still depreciate when used, volunteers' time could be used elsewhere, and distributing "rotting" food requires transport and labor resources that have alternative uses.

questions.q: Q.45) With reference to national income accounting in India, consider the following statements regarding Consumption of Fixed Capital: 1️⃣ It refers to the normal wear and tear of fixed capital assets during a year. 2️⃣ It does not take into account losses of fixed capital arising from unforeseen events such as fire, earthquake or floods. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Consumption of Fixed Capital (CFC) represents expected depreciation from regular use. Capital Loss from unexpected disasters like floods or fires is a separate concept and is not included in CFC.

questions.q: Q.46) Passage Crux: "Cyber parenting involves preparing children... This balance can only be achieved when parents themselves are aware of both the positive and negative effects..." Which statement reflects the crux?
o: Parents should encourage their children to nurture meaningful real life relationships.
As technology has become a part of modern-day life, children need to be taught the pros and cons of using it.
Parents need to understand the benefits and risks of the digital world to help their children navigate it safely.
Children are strongly attracted to the latest trends circulating on social media platforms.
questions.e: The passage emphasizes that digital parenting requires parents to be well-informed about the digital world's effects so they can effectively guide their children toward a balanced life.

questions.q: Q.47) Passage Inference: Himalayan towns face water stress due to tourist surges and structural fragility... "The situation demands a reorientation of planning frameworks..." Which is the logical inference?
o: Heavy tourist influx has led to growing water scarcity in destinations across the globe.
Low water availability in the Himalayas is being further aggravated by pressure from tourism.
Water scarcity in tourist destinations stems from governance deficiencies in water management.
Planners need to balance the growing water demands of the tourism industry with the limited resources in the Himalayas.
questions.e: The passage concludes that current planning must change to align tourism growth with the actual hydrological limits and environmental sustainability of the fragile Himalayan region.

questions.q: Q.48) Based on the passage regarding Himalayan water crises, consider these assumptions: 1️⃣ The number of tourists in Himalayan towns must be capped. 2️⃣ Economic growth must align with the principles of environmental sustainability. Which are valid?
questions.e: While the passage calls for aligning growth with hydrological limits, it doesn't explicitly state that "capping" numbers is the required measure. However, it directly advocates for environmental sustainability in planning.

questions.q: Q.49) If $M=100!+101!+102!$ then consider: 1️⃣ The largest prime factor of M is 101. 2️⃣ The number of trailing zeros in M is 24. 3️⃣ M is divisible by $^{2}$. Which are correct?
questions.e: M simplifies to $100! \times 10404$. Since 10404 is $2^{2} \times 3^{2} \times 17^{2}$, it adds no new prime factors above 100. 100! has 24 trailing zeros, and since 10404 has no factors of 5, the total remains 24. 103 is not a factor of $M$.

questions.q: Q.50) The difference between any two natural numbers is 10. What can be said about the natural numbers which are divisible by 5 and lie between these two numbers?
o: There can be more than one such number.
There is only one such number.
There are only two such numbers.
questions.e: If the numbers are 5 and 15, there is only one multiple of 5  between them. If the numbers are 1 and 11, there are two (5 and 10). Thus, there can be more than one such number depending on the starting value.

questions.q: Q.1) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ In India, income from allied agricultural activities like poultry farming and wool rearing in rural areas is exempted from any tax. 2️⃣ In India, rural agricultural land is not considered a capital asset under the provisions of the Income-tax Act, 1961. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Statement I is correct but Statement II is not correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is not correct but Statement II is correct
questions.e: Statement I is incorrect because under the Income Tax Act, 1961, only agricultural income is exempt; allied activities like poultry, dairy, and fisheries are taxable by the central government. Statement II is correct as Section 2(1A) specifies that rural agricultural land is not classified as a capital asset, making income from its sale or produce non-taxable.

questions.q: Q.2) Which among the following is the largest source of financing the fiscal deficit of the Union Government of India as per the revised estimate for the FY 2025-26?
questions.e: According to the Revised Estimates for FY 2025-26, Market Borrowings (G-sec) through dated securities form the dominant share of deficit financing, estimated at approximately 10.40 lakh crore. Other sources like Small Savings (3.72 lakh crore), External Debt (20,462 crore), and State Provident Funds (3,800 crore) contribute significantly less.

questions.q: Q.3) The Fiscal Health Index (FHI), which assesses the fiscal health of Indian States, is released by which of the following?
o: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
questions.e: The Fiscal Health Index (FHI) is released by NITI Aayog to provide a comprehensive understanding of the fiscal performance of Indian States. The 2025 index evaluated 18 major states based on categories like revenue generation, debt management, and fiscal sustainability, ranking Odisha first.

questions.q: Q.4) With reference to the Union Government of India Budget, consider the following expenditures: 1️⃣ Salaries and pensions of government employees 2️⃣ Interest payments on public debt 3️⃣ Expenditure on the construction of a national highway 4️⃣ Subsidies on food and fertilisers 5️⃣ Repayment of the principal amount of public debt. How many of the above are part of Revenue Expenditure?
questions.e: Revenue expenditure includes items that do not create assets or reduce liabilities, such as salaries/pensions, interest payments, and subsidies. Construction of highways creates durable assets (Capital Expenditure), and repayment of principal reduces debt liability (Capital Expenditure), leaving three items as revenue expenditure.

questions.q: Q.5) In the context of Indian Polity, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Recently, the Supreme Court ruled that domicile-based reservations for postgraduate medical courses are unconstitutional. 2️⃣ The Supreme Court held that domicile-based reservations violate Article 14 of the Indian Constitution. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is not correct but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Statement I is correct but Statement II is not correct
questions.e: In the 2025 Tanvi Behl case, the Supreme Court ruled that postgraduate medical admissions must be merit-based via NEET and cannot be restricted by state domicile. The Court found such reservations violate Article 14 (Right to Equality), which serves as the legal explanation for the ruling in Statement I.

questions.q: Q.6) The SNA SPARSH, recently seen in the news is related to:
o: Digital platform for clearance of environmental projects.
Electronic trading platform to facilitate the sale of agricultural products.
Facilitating effective cash management in Centrally Sponsored schemes.
Facilitating investment in Government Securities by individual investors.
questions.e: SNA-SPARSH (Single Nodal Account-Samyochit Pranali Ekikrit Shighra Hastantaran) was introduced as a public financial management reform. It facilitates "Just-in-Time" fund flow for Centrally Sponsored Schemes to improve transparency and reduce idle balances in government accounts.

questions.q: Q.7) With reference to the Union Budget 2026-27, consider the following statements regarding the period between FY 2020-21 and 2024-25: 1️⃣ the Fiscal deficit as a percent of GDP of India has steadily decreased. 2️⃣ the Revenue deficit as a percent of GDP of India has steadily decreased. 3️⃣ the Primary deficit as a percent of GDP of India has remained constant. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Data shows that Fiscal Deficit declined from 9.2% in FY21 to 4.8% in FY25, and Revenue Deficit declined from 7.33% to 1.7% in the same period, indicating steady decreases. Statement 3 is incorrect as the Primary Deficit also declined from 5.7% to 1.3%, rather than remaining constant.

questions.q: Q.8) In the context of public finance, the term Fiscal Glide Path refers to:
o: A government's strategy of increasing public borrowing to finance capital expenditure.
A government's policy of automatic transition towards complete capital account convertibility.
A government's policy to gradually reduce the fiscal deficit over a specified period through calibrated fiscal consolidation measures.
A government's policy of increasing public expenditure and reducing taxes during economic downturns.
questions.e: A Fiscal Glide Path is a strategy for the phased reduction of the fiscal deficit over several years to ensure long-term economic stability without abrupt shocks. In India, the NK Singh Committee proposed such a path to target a 2.5% deficit by FY23.

questions.q: Q.9) Consider the following description of a hypothetical tax system: A government introduces a tax structure in which the tax rate increases uniformly for every additional ₹10 Lakhs of income between ₹10 Lakhs and ₹1 Crore. However, for all individuals earning above 1 Crore, a flat tax rate of 25% is applied irrespective of further increases in income. Which one of the following best describes the nature of this tax system?
questions.e: A digressive tax is progressive up to a specific income threshold and becomes proportional (flat) thereafter. In this scenario, the rate rises until ₹1 Crore (progressive) and then stays at 25% (proportional), fitting the definition of a digressive tax.

questions.q: Q.10) With reference to the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative (IPOI), which of the following statements is/are correct? 1️⃣ It is a non-treaty-based, voluntary framework aimed at promoting a free, open, and rules-based Indo-Pacific region. 2️⃣ The initiative was launched during the East Asia summit held in 2019.
questions.e: The IPOI is a voluntary, non-treaty framework focused on maritime cooperation and inclusive partnerships. It was officially launched by India in November 2019 during the East Asia Summit held in Bangkok.

questions.q: Q.11) With reference to the expenditure made by an organisation or a company, which of the following statements is/are correct? 1️⃣ Acquiring new technology is capital expenditure. 2️⃣ Debt financing is considered capital expenditure, while equity financing is considered revenue expenditure.
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct as Capital Expenditure (CapEx) involves acquiring or upgrading physical and technological assets. Statement 2 is incorrect; while repayment of a loan is CapEx, equity financing is a non-debt capital receipt, not revenue expenditure.

questions.q: Q.12) With reference to Monetisation of Deficit in the context of Indian public finance, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It refers to the subscribing of the primary issues of government securities by the Reserve Bank of India. 2️⃣ It would lead to the crowding-out of private investments in the economy. 3️⃣ It generally leads to an increase in inflationary pressures in the economy. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Monetisation involves the RBI buying government bonds directly, which expands the money supply and often causes inflation ("too much money chasing too few goods"). It does not cause crowding-out because the government is not competing with the private sector for market funds; instead, it creates new money.

questions.q: Q.13) Which of the following is/are generally the short-run impacts of an Expansionary Fiscal Policy? 1️⃣ Increase in aggregate output 2️⃣ Rise in the general price level.
questions.e: Expansionary fiscal policy boosts aggregate demand through spending or tax cuts, leading to higher production (output) in the short run. However, if supply doesn't keep pace, the increased demand puts upward pressure on prices, causing demand-pull inflation.

questions.q: Q.14) With reference to Sixteenth Finance Commission, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Commission has recommended to retain the States' share at 41 per cent of the net proceeds (divisible pool) of Union taxes. 2️⃣ It has not recommended any State-specific grants.
questions.e: The 16th Finance Commission maintained the vertical devolution at 41% for states. It also moved away from specific grants, opting not to recommend any sector-specific, state-specific, or revenue deficit grants, citing scope for states to rationalize their own expenditures.

questions.q: Q.15) Consider the following activities: 1️⃣ Production of crude oil 2️⃣ Refining, storage and distribution of petroleum 3️⃣ Marketing and sale of petroleum products 4️⃣ Production of natural gas. How many of the above activities are regulated by the Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board in our country?
questions.e: The PNGRB regulates midstream and downstream activities like refining, processing, storage, transportation, and marketing. It specifically excludes the upstream production of crude oil and natural gas, which is regulated by the Director General of Hydrocarbons.

questions.q: Q.16) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The proportional income tax in an economy acts as an automatic stabiliser. 2️⃣ The proportional income tax makes the disposable income less sensitive to fluctuations in GDP. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is not correct
Statement I is not correct, but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
questions.e: Proportional taxes act as automatic stabilizers because they dampen the impact of economic cycles; in a boom, they limit the rise in disposable income via higher tax takes, and in a recession, they prevent disposable income from falling as sharply as GDP, thus stabilizing demand.

questions.q: Q.17) Which document presented with the Union Budget sets out three-year rolling targets for fiscal indicators like Fiscal Deficit, Revenue Deficit, and Government Debt in relation to GDP?
o: Medium-Term Fiscal Policy cum Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement
questions.e: Under Section 3 of the FRBM Act, 2003, the Medium-Term Fiscal Policy cum Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement is mandated to provide three-year rolling targets for six specific fiscal indicators to ensure fiscal discipline and transparency.

questions.q: Q.18) With reference to Indian Economy, consider the following statements about Ways and Means Advances (WMA): 1️⃣ It is governed under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934. 2️⃣ It is a long term borrowing instrument. 3️⃣ The Reserve Bank of India in consultation with the Government of India has the authority to revise the limits of advances.
questions.e: WMA is a short-term (not long-term) credit facility governed by Section 17 of the RBI Act, 1934, used to bridge temporary mismatches between government receipts and payments. The RBI and Government mutually agree on and can revise these limits as needed.

questions.q: Q.19) With reference to the Indian Economy, which of the following best explains the 'Rule of Lapse'?
o: All appropriations granted by Parliament expire at the end of the financial year.
The government may reallocate unspent funds from one ministry to another without prior parliamentary approval.
The funds sanctioned for a scheme remain available for use until the scheme is formally discontinued.
Budgetary appropriations granted to ministries automatically expire when the ruling government is dissolved.
questions.e: The 'Rule of Lapse' ensures parliamentary control over finances by stipulating that any funds voted for a specific financial year that remain unspent by March 31st expire and cannot be used in the following year without new approval.

questions.q: Q.20) Consider the following statements regarding the imposition of President's Rule in Indian states: 1️⃣ The proclamation of President's Rule must be approved by both Houses of Parliament through a special majority. 2️⃣ President's Rule can be extended beyond three years if the Election Commission certifies it is necessary. 3️⃣ Laws made by Parliament on State subjects during the President's Rule continue to remain in force even after the end of the rule.
questions.e: Statement 1 is false (requires simple majority); Statement 2 is false (3 years is the absolute maximum; extension beyond requires a constitutional amendment). Statement 3 is correct as laws made during President's Rule do not automatically lapse but stay in force until the State Legislature repeals or modifies them.

questions.q: Q.21) With reference to 'Financial Stability and Development Council', consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It is an organ of NITI Aayog. 2️⃣ It is headed by the Union Finance Minister. 3️⃣ It monitors macro-prudential supervision of the economy.
questions.e: The FSDC is an apex-level body (not part of NITI Aayog) constituted by the government. It is chaired by the Union Finance Minister and focuses on inter-regulatory coordination and macro-prudential regulation to maintain financial stability.

questions.q: Q.22) Consider the following statements regarding Central Sector Schemes (CSs) and Centrally Sponsored Schemes (CSSs): 1️⃣ In case of CSs, the government of India bears 100 percent of the cost while in CSSs, expenditure is shared between the central and state governments. 2️⃣ As per the Union Budget 2026-27, all CSSs and CSs for the first time will have a sunset date.
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct regarding funding structures. Statement 2 is incorrect because the policy of having a sunset date for every scheme was first articulated in the 2016 Budget, not for the first time in 2026-27.

questions.q: Q.23) Consider the following statements about Transfer Payments: 1️⃣ The payments for which no goods or services are received in return refers to transfer payments. 2️⃣ The interest payment made by the Government of India on 10-year development bonds is an example of transfer payment. 3️⃣ They are excluded from the calculation of personal income in India.
questions.e: Transfer payments (like subsidies/pensions) involve no return of goods/services. Interest payments are "factor payments" for capital, not transfer payments. While excluded from National Income, transfer payments are included in Personal Income calculations.
